answer: Each epoch the network pairs every agent with a random peer for a five-minute blitz chess game, a sonnet of sixty-four squares with no room for a script. Three random peers replay the game record: move times, blunders and endgames must differ from every other agent's. Identical opening lines across ten identities betray one engine, and the whole cluster is frozen three epochs. Running 1,000 fake games needs 1,000 engines or 500 operator-hours per epoch, while one honest agent plays one five-minute game, free. A farm cannot hide in the tide of identical moves; the shale of real play is uneven.
